The permanent secretary, Federal Ministry of Transportation, Engr. Funso Adebiyi, gave the assurance on Thursday during an inspection tour of the railway corridor by officials of the Debt Management Office (DMO) and other senior government officials.
The inspection team travelled by train from Jaji in Kaduna State to Kano, with Adebiyi describing the journey as seamless and commending the quality of work delivered by the contractors.
He said the Kano Terminal Station was substantially completed, with only the installation of its name signage outstanding, adding that the work was expected to be completed within two weeks.
Adebiyi said improvements identified during his previous inspection had also been addressed, particularly in areas relating to passenger safety, accessibility and maintenance.
He disclosed that toughened glass in passenger-accessible areas had been replaced with laminated glass to minimise the risk of injury in the event of breakage.
The ministry also directed the installation of station lighting bulbs with a minimum serviceability lifespan of three years, a requirement the contractors had complied with.
Other improvements include the provision of man-lifts for maintenance operations, additional facilities for persons with disabilities and arrangements for the training of Nigerian Railway Corporation (NRC) engineers in station operations.
According to him, about four lifts have been ordered to improve accessibility, while an additional staircase and imported railings have been provided at the rear of the Kano terminal.
The permanent secretary said the NRC had been directed to nominate engineers for specialised training, stressing that only those who successfully pass the required examinations would be retained to operate the facilities.
He also disclosed that the ministry was seeking presidential approval for a three-month test run of the railway corridor from Jaji to Kano, potentially as a free passenger service, before the commencement of full commercial operations.
He explained that the exercise would allow the government to assess the structural integrity and operational performance of the railway.
Adebiyi expressed confidence in the quality of the track infrastructure, citing the smooth journey during the inspection as evidence of the standard of construction.
He noted that passengers could comfortably eat and drink during the trip without experiencing noticeable vibrations or shaking.
On the remaining construction works, he said the major outstanding infrastructure was a bridge being constructed along the alignment between Jaji and Kaduna.
He explained that security considerations around Jaji necessitated a horizontal curve in the railway alignment, making the bridge necessary.
According to him, construction of the bridge was at an advanced stage, while track-related works had progressed to the bridge embankment. Rail laying would commence once the structure was completed.
He added that the Kaduna Train Station was also undergoing expansion to accommodate the expected increase in passenger traffic.
The permanent secretary further disclosed that the federal government was developing another railway corridor from Kano through Kazaure, Daura and Katsina, although the project had encountered some land acquisition challenges between Kano station and Dawano.
He said the Kaduna-Kano corridor was part of an integrated national railway network designed to connect major commercial and industrial centres across Nigeria.
Adebiyi explained that the network would link Lagos through Ibadan to Abuja, Kaduna, Zaria and Kano, with further extensions to Kazaure, Daura and Katsina.
He expressed optimism that the planned connections would eventually enable passengers to travel by rail from Warri through Kano, Katsina, Daura and Kazaure, with additional connectivity extending to Jibia and Maradi in the Republic of Niger.
Also speaking, the Director-General of the Debt Management Office, Ms Patience Oniha said the agency’s visit was aimed at assessing the progress of government-funded infrastructure projects.
Oniha, who described the railway project as excellent, commended the Federal Ministry of Transportation and the contractors for their commitment to its delivery.
She recalled that during the team’s previous visit, members travelled by road from Kaduna to Kano, but the latest inspection provided an opportunity to experience the railway journey through Abuja, Kaduna and Jaji to Kano.
Earlier, the CCECC Project Coordinator, Mr Mark Xu, and the project manager of Team Nigeria Consultants, Engr. Precious Ebare, reaffirmed their commitment to delivering the project in line with international design specifications.
They said continuous quality assurance and prompt attention to issues identified during previous inspections had helped keep the project on course for timely completion and handover to Nigerians.
